Methods
and
Materials

To
determine
whether
the
sewage
effluent
inhibits
or
enhances

bacterial
and
diatomaceous
films ,
six
stations
were
established

seaward
of
the
Pacific
Grove
intertidal
outfall .
The
stations

( Fig .
1 ) ,
were
located
approximately
10
meters
apart
for
a
total

distance
of
approximately
65
meters
away
from
the
outfall
mouth .

Stations
were
chosen
that
were
similar
in
terms
of
tidal
height ,

wave
shock ,
light
and
spatial
orientation .

Since
the
study
was
of
short
duration
and
microscopic
organisms

were
being
investigated ,
I
felt
2 "
x
2 "
glass
lantern
slides
( Semon

Bache
&
Co. ,
Spec .
# 75-356 )
would
provide
an
adequate
settling
surface

for
bacteria ,
diatoms
and
any
chance
maroinvertebrate
larvae

settling
out .
Dr.
Eugene
Haderlie ,
of
the
U.S.
Naval
Post - Graduate

School ,
Monterey
Ca. ,
in
his
studies
( Haderlie
1968 ,
1970 ) ,
has

shown
the
choice
of
settlement
surface
to
be
inconsequential .

Oak
holding
frames
( Fig .
2 ) ,
were
constructed
to
secure
the
slides
in

the
intertidal
area .
The
1/4 "
x
2 '
x
6 "
frames
were
secured
to
granite

x
21
x
6

boulders
at
the
six
stations ,
the
first
of
which
was
located
three

feet
directly
north
of
the
outfall
mouth .
All
frames
were
secured

at
the
0.0
tide
level
and
on
the
rock
face
opposite
prevalent
wave

direction .
Holes
were
drilled
by
star
drill
and
hammer
and
the
frames

attached
by
expanding
lead
plugs
and
2 "
x
1/4 "
lag
bolts .
Twenty-

four
slides
for
each
station
were
boiled
in
nitric
acid
and
autoclaved

at
250 ° F
for
15
minutes .
The
slides
were
placed
in
their
respective

racks
on
April
30th .
One
slide
from
each
station
was
recovered
daily

for
the
following
two
days .
These
preliminary
plates
showed
a
great

abundance
of
bacteria
of
various
morphologic
types .
To
better

characterize
bacteria
accumulating ,
the
standard
Gram
stain
test

was
chosen .

After
six
days
exposure ,
the
slides ,
though
appearing
clean
to
the

unaided
eye ,
contained
a
remarkable
assemblage
of
microscopic
organisms .

To
follow
the
very
early
stages
of
microbial
succession ,
five
new

plates
were
placed
in
the
frames ,
and
one
plate
removed
successively

for
the
following
five
days .
This
phase
of
experiment ,
designated

Short
Term
Study
1
( STS - 1 ) ,
was
duplicated
by
Short
Term
Study
2

( STS - 2 ) .
Plates
originally
placed
in
the
frames
were
left
for

Long
Term
analyses .
